title: Efficient Conversion of Optical to Mechanical States Close to the Single-Quantum Level
authors: Alexander Rolf Korsch, Liu Chen, Pedro V. Pinho, Boris Müllendorff, Jan N. Kirchhof, Yong Yu, Thiago P. Mayer Alegre, Simon Gröblacher
abstract: Coherent interfaces between optical photons and mechanical excitations provide a promising route towards phonon-state engineering and hybrid quantum information processing. Cavity optomechanical systems enable such interfaces via optomechanically induced transparency (OMIT), allowing coherent mapping between traveling optical fields and localized mechanical modes. However, previous implementations of OMIT conversion protocols were limited to classical input signals with large coherent state photon numbers due to room temperature operation and corresponding thermal mechanical noise. Here, we demonstrate efficient low-noise photon-phonon state transfer close to the single-quantum regime in an optomechanical crystal operated at Millikelvin temperatures. Using weak coherent optical input pulses at the few-photon level, we achieve a record-level photon-phonon conversion efficiency of $η=0.76$, a mechanical storage lifetime of $T_\mathrm{1}=7.3~μs$, and a tunable conversion bandwidth exceeding 4.5 MHz. Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurements of the retrieved signal demonstrate the coherent nature of the converted phononic state, evidencing low added thermal noise in the conversion process ($n_\mathrm{th}=9.0$). These results establish optomechanical crystals as efficient optical interfaces to GHz mechanical modes and provide a pathway toward deterministic single-quantum-level mechanical state preparation.
summary: This paper reports on the efficient, low-noise conversion of quantum optical photons into mechanical phonons using an optomechanical crystal operating at millikelvin temperatures. By utilizing the OMIT mechanism with few-photon inputs, the researchers achieved a high conversion efficiency ($\eta=0.76$) and confirmed the quantum nature of the stored mechanical state. This work advances the field by providing a robust pathway toward deterministic single-quantum mechanical state preparation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to achieve efficient, low-noise conversion of quantum optical states (photons) into quantum mechanical states (phonons) near the single-quantum level.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a record-level photon-phonon conversion efficiency of $\eta=0.76$ while maintaining low added thermal noise ($n_{th}=9.0$), establishing the platform for deterministic single-quantum mechanical state preparation.
method: The conversion is achieved using Optomechanically Induced Transparency (OMIT) in a cavity optomechanical crystal, probing the system with weak, few-photon coherent optical pulses.
model_or_system: The system utilizes a quasi-two-dimensional optomechanical crystal (OMC) operating at millikelvin temperatures. The interaction is modeled via an effective beam-splitter Hamiltonian, enabling coherent mapping between optical fields and mechanical modes.
key_observables: Conversion efficiency ($\eta$), mechanical storage lifetime ($T_1$), added thermal noise ($n_{th}$), and the second-order autocorrelation function $g^{(2)}(\Delta n)$ of the retrieved phononic state.
important_parameters: Millikelvin temperatures, few-photon input pulses, mechanical frequency ($\Omega_m/2\pi = 10.314$ GHz), and the coupling strength ($g_0/2\pi = 1.0$ MHz).
main_assumptions: The process relies on operating in the resolved-sideband regime and requires low temperatures to suppress thermal noise, which was a limitation in previous room-temperature efforts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the OMIT mechanism, the experimental setup involving two optical paths, and diagnostic measurements like the HBT autocorrelation function $g^{(2)}(\Delta n)$ to confirm the quantum nature of the converted state.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework using OMIT, presents the experimental setup and measurements of the OMIT window, and culminates in demonstrating the high-efficiency, low-noise quantum state transfer from photons to phonons.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interface between quantum optics and mechanical oscillators, which is a cornerstone of modern AMO physics, particularly in quantum transducers and quantum memory.
